holidays.name: National Cosmopolitan Day
holidays.description: Raise a chilled martini glass to the pink, citrusy cocktail that made vodka and cranberry juice glamorous. Today is the day to shake one up with lime and orange liqueur, and to garnish it with a flamed orange peel if you're feeling fancy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance dedicated to the Cosmopolitan cocktail. The drink rose to fame in the late 1980s and 1990s, and bartender Toby Cecchini's 1988 New York version helped shape the modern recipe.
holidays.funFact: The Cosmopolitan became a pop-culture icon in the late 1990s after it showed up constantly in the hands of the characters on Sex and the City.

holidays.name: National Roast Leg of Lamb Day
holidays.description: A day for the carnivorous showstopper of the dinner table. Think garlic, rosemary, and a golden-crusted leg of lamb roasting in the oven until the whole house smells amazing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a classic centerpiece dish that has been served at festive meals for centuries.
holidays.funFact: Roast leg of lamb is a traditional spring feast in many cultures, and it's especially linked with Easter and Passover-season tables.

holidays.name: Paste Up Day
holidays.description: A salute to the sticky art of the paste-up. Slap some wheatpaste on a wall, or just cut, glue, and collage to your heart's content. Posters, zines, and street art all count.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It nods to the DIY paste-up tradition used in street art, flyering, and old-school print layout.
holidays.funFact: Before desktop publishing, newspapers and magazines were laid out by hand. Designers literally pasted strips of text and images onto boards before printing.
